deepdive.sec: Textiles / Integrated Denim, Yarn & Garment Manufacturer

bull_bear.body: Prioritizing debt reduction (INR100-120cr/year repayment); no dividend policy mentioned; focus on maximizing ROI from existing capex; no M&A or new verticals planned; ROCE target: 12% within 12-18 months
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Cotton price volatility (30-35% import reliance temporarily); U.S. apparel tariffs (indirect exposure via customers); global demand slowdown; no pricing pressure from Bangladesh/China; no material inventory markdowns
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and operationally focused; emphasizes sustainability, efficiency, and capital discipline; dismisses near-term macro risks; avoids overpromising on margins or capex; transparent on one-offs
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite INR23cr PAT, normalized PAT is ~INR14cr after depreciation one-off; 70% of power to be renewable in 15-18 months (from 15% today); garment division’s 35% utilization is a turnaround from 4 straight quarters of decline; export revenue not impacted by U.S. tariffs due to routing via Bangladesh/Africa
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Cotton yarn: 90%+ utilization; Denim/PV fabric: 85-90% utilization, 10-15% upside; Garments: 35% utilization, targeting 60-65% in Q3; EBITDA margins range 8-12% across segments; working capital cycle: 30-45 days longer for fabric vs yarn
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U.S. apparel tariffs | Indian apparel exporters | loser | High | Sangam avoids direct exposure via fabric/yarn exports routed through Bangladesh/Africa, unlike pure-play garment exporters |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin expansion driven by: 1) Bottomed-out cotton/yarn prices (Q1 to Q2: +2-3% yarn price increase, cycle stabilized); 2) Higher capacity utilization; 3) Newer, more efficient capex assets; 4) Product mix shift toward higher-margin items; 5) Upcoming INR10cr/year savings from 12MW captive solar (Dec 2025)
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 12-15% FY26; EBITDA margin: Targeting 11-12% in next 2 quarters; Order inflow: Stable export mix (35-40%); Capex/commissioning: No major capex planned; maintenance capex: INR50-70cr/year; 12MW captive solar to commission Dec 2025
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Garment division order book has improved significantly; utilization up to 35% from 25% last quarter; expected to reach 60-65% next quarter; other divisions operating near full capacity
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Garment division capacity utilization to rise to 60-65% in next 2 quarters; potential for 10-12% further utilization gain in denim/fabric; export market stability (35-40% of revenue); no major capex planned, organic growth from utilization and mix
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Sangam has completed its multi-year capex cycle, driving volume growth and margin expansion through higher capacity utilization and improved product mix; the one-time depreciation policy change boosted PAT, but underlying EBITDA margin growth of 120 bps to 9.6% is sustainable and supported by operational efficiencies and falling raw material costs.

meta.thesis: Sangam has completed its multi-year capex cycle, driving volume growth and margin expansion through higher capacity utilization and improved product mix; the one-time depreciation policy change boosted PAT, but underlying EBITDA margin growth of 120 bps to 9.6% is sustainable and supported by operational efficiencies and falling raw material costs.
